description: The configuration surface of the cloud-shell chart. GENERATED from values.yaml by `./build.sh Charts` and diffed in CI — docs/plan/03 § charts/. Edit values.yaml, never this file. Members carrying `x-cybercloud-api: false` are chart or platform plumbing and are not part of the resource body.

audit.description: docs/plan/19 § Auditing. Who, when, from where, which subscription and for how long is always recorded and is not a setting.

sessionRecording.description: Whether everything typed into and printed by this shell is recorded. ⚠ Off by default and immutable afterwards: a shell contains secrets, a keystroke log is a liability, and a recording that could be switched off mid-life would be worth nothing to the compliance requirement it exists for.

ephemeralStorageLimit.description: How much a shell may write outside its home volume.
ephemeralStorageLimit.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Not a tenant choice, because the failure it prevents is the NODE'S rather than the tenant's: an unbounded emptyDir fills the kubelet's disk and evicts every pod on the machine, including other tenants'.

home.description: The persistent home directory. The only part of a console that survives an idle reclaim.

retentionDays.description: How long $HOME is kept after the console was last attached to. ⚠ Nothing sweeps on it yet — it is carried so that a console created today is swept correctly by whatever does.

size.description: The size of $HOME. It grows and never shrinks: a PersistentVolumeClaim refuses a decrease at the API.

principalId.description: The managed identity every command in this shell acts as. It may not be changed: a console whose identity moved would have an audit trail describing a shell that no longer exists.

variant.description: default carries every tool in docs/plan/19's table and takes about 40 seconds to pull cold; minimal carries shells, editors, cyc and kubectl and starts in about 8. The repository and the digest are the platform's.

imageRepository.description: Where the shell image is published.
imageRepository.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: A tenant choosing what runs in a pod that holds their own managed identity is the whole attack, so the image is the platform's and not a setting. ⚠ NOTHING IN THIS REPOSITORY BUILDS IT — build/Build.Images.cs publishes .NET hosts through the SDK's container tooling and its header forbids a Dockerfile, and a 2.5 GB shell image is neither. conformance.yaml § owed, `no-image-pipeline`.

nameOverride.description: Replace the generated object-name stem. Empty means derive it from the release name.
nameOverride.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Helm plumbing. Nothing about it belongs in a resource body.

network.description: What the shell may reach. Nothing may ever reach the shell.

egress.description: Internet lets the shell reach public addresses as well as this subscription's own workloads and DNS — a shell that cannot git clone is not a shell. TenantOnly removes the public half and leaves the rest.

platform.description: Resource identity injected by the reconciler. Not a tenant-facing setting.

apiVersion.description: The api-version the resource was last written at, rendered into the cybercloud.io/api-version label.
apiVersion.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

managedBy.description: Value of the cybercloud.io/managed-by label. Constant, and the selector every informer filters on.
managedBy.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

namespace.description: The resource's own namespace, which the network policy allows the shell to reach.
namespace.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceGroup.description: Resource group name, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-group label.
resourceGroup.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceId.description: Resource GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-id label.
resourceId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceType.description: Fully qualified resource type, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-type label and into the network policy's own podSelector.
resourceType.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

subscriptionId.description: Subscription GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/subscription-id label.
subscriptionId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

tenantId.description: Tenant GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/tenant-id label AND into the network policy's tenant-wide egress selector. ⚠ It is the only value in this file that is both an identity label and a security control.
tenantId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

platform.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

session.description: When a shell stops. Both numbers are ceilings a tenant may lower and neither may be turned off.

idleTimeoutMinutes.description: How long a shell may sit with nobody typing into it before it is reclaimed. The home volume survives; the pod does not. ⚠ There is no value meaning never — an idle terminal is a tenant paying for something they closed.

maxDurationHours.description: The longest a single shell may run, busy or not. Enforced by the kubelet through the pod's own deadline, so it holds even when nothing of this platform is running.

sizing.description: CPU and memory for the shell.

preset.description: How much a shell gets. The ladder stops at 2 vCPU and 4 GiB, which is docs/plan/19's ceiling for this row — a workload that needs more needs a cluster and a job rather than a terminal.
